items.followUp: What is meant by problem analysis?

rubric.why: The answer identifies that defining a problem involves understanding it.
rubric.description: Explains that the problem must be understood clearly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the problem is clearly understood.

rubric.why: Identifying what goes into a problem and what result is required helps define it.
rubric.description: Mentions identifying the problem’s inputs and required output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning inputs and outputs, with or without processing.

modelAnswer: Defining the problem means clearly understanding and stating the problem to be solved.
It includes identifying the required input, processing and output.

items.followUp: What is an algorithm, and how can it be checked?

rubric.why: A trace table records how variable values change as an algorithm runs.
rubric.description: States that a trace table records variable values during execution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the recording of variable values.

rubric.why: Tracing helps check whether an algorithm behaves correctly and can reveal errors.
rubric.description: Gives the purpose of checking an algorithm or finding errors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning checking correctness, logic or errors.

modelAnswer: A trace table is used to record the values of variables as an algorithm is executed.
It helps check the logic and correctness of the algorithm and find errors.

items.followUp: What is meant by a test case?

rubric.why: Test data is supplied to a program to test it.
rubric.description: Defines test data as data used to test a program.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that data is used to test a program.

rubric.why: Test data helps check whether the program produces the correct result.
rubric.description: States that test data is used to check the program’s result or correctness.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning checking the expected result or correctness.

modelAnswer: Test data is input data used to test a program.
The results are checked to determine whether the program works correctly.

items.followUp: What are paired HTML tags? Give one example.

rubric.why: A singular tag does not have a corresponding closing tag.
rubric.description: Defines singular tags as tags without a closing tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a singular tag has no closing tag.

rubric.why: BR, HR and IMG are examples of singular HTML tags.
rubric.description: Provides a valid example of a singular tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid example.

modelAnswer: Singular tags are HTML tags that do not have a separate closing tag.

rubric.why: Online piracy involves copying or using material without authorization.
rubric.description: States that piracy involves unauthorized or illegal copying.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying unauthorized copying or use.

rubric.why: The question asks about piracy carried out online, commonly involving copyrighted material.
rubric.description: Connects the unauthorized copying or distribution to the internet or online copyrighted material.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the internet or online distribution of copyrighted material.

modelAnswer: Online piracy is the unauthorized copying, downloading or distribution of copyrighted material through the internet.
It may involve software, music, movies or other digital content.

rubric.why: The repeated division-by-2 method gives the binary digits from the remainders.
rubric.description: Shows a valid division-by-2 conversion or its correct remainders.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct conversion method, including the remainder sequence.

rubric.why: The correct binary representation of decimal 156 is 10011100.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer.

rubric.why: A bit is a binary digit.
rubric.description: Identifies a bit as a binary digit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a bit is a binary digit.

rubric.why: A bit can have either of the two binary values.
rubric.description: Gives the possible values of a bit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a bit is either 0 or 1.

modelAnswer: A bit is a binary digit, the smallest unit of data in a computer.
